title: ては and ても
summary: ても means "even if" and joins two clauses without taking sides; ては points at an unwelcome result and shrinks to ちゃ in casual speech.

blocks.text: Both endings sit after the **て-form** and add a particle. Notice which particle: **も** is the "also / even" particle, and **は** is the topic particle that draws a line around something. Their personalities come straight from that.
ても: even if, even though

も says "even as far as that". 雨が降っても means "even going as far as rain". The result that follows is simply not stopped by it, and it can be good or bad. This is the same も that appears in でも, where で is the て-form of だ.

blocks.jp: 雨が降っても公園に行く。
blocks.en: Even if it rains, I will go to the park.
Even though it is cold, I go for a walk.

blocks.text: Turn ても into a question and you have permission: "even if I did that, would it be fine?"

blocks.jp: ここに座ってもいいですか。

blocks.text: ては: that would be a problem

は narrows things down: **"as soon as you do just this"**. The result tends to be **unwelcome**: a ban, a complaint, a trouble. Because it is so often used to forbid, casual speech squeezes ては into **ちゃ** (and では into **じゃ**).

blocks.jp: 雨が降っては遠足に行けない。
blocks.en: If it rains, we cannot go on the trip (and that is a nuisance).

blocks.jp: ここで泣いては恥ずかしい。
blocks.en: It would be embarrassing to cry here.

blocks.jp: ここで寝ちゃだめだよ。

items: **て-form + も**: even if / even though, any kind of result.
**て-form + は**: when that happens, trouble; often forbids.
**ては → ちゃ**, **では → じゃ** in casual speech.

questions.prompt: 雨が降＿＿、公園に行く。 (Even if it rains, I will go.)
先生、帰ってもいいですか。
questions.note: て-form + もいい asks for permission.

questions.prompt: ここで笑っちゃだめだよ。
questions.note: ちゃ is the casual form of ては, and it forbids.

questions.instruction: Which is the casual contraction of 食べては?
questions.note: ては → ちゃ after a verb like 食べる.

questions.prompt: ては usually points to an unwelcome result.
questions.note: は draws the line: just doing that is already a problem.

questions.instruction: What mood does ては give this sentence?
questions.prompt: 雨が降っては遠足に行けない。
options: The rain is an unwelcome obstacle
The rain is a welcome gift
Nothing; the sentence is neutral good news
It is a question about rain
questions.note: ては: that situation causes trouble.

options: Even though it is cold, I go for a walk
Because it is cold, I stay home
If it is cold, I will not walk
It is cold, so I took a walk
questions.note: ても: the result is not stopped by the cold.

questions.prompt: Even if it rains, I will go to the park.
questions.note: Condition first, then the main verb.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that sets up an unwelcome "if I did that"
questions.note: 泣いては: ては points at the trouble to come.

questions.instruction: In 空っぽのびんでも, what is で?
questions.note: でも = で (て-form of だ) + も: even though it is an empty jar.

questions.prompt: ここに座っ＿＿いいですか。 (May I sit here?)
questions.note: Permission is て-form + もいい.

questions.prompt: ても can only be used when the result is bad.
questions.note: ても joins any contrast; it takes no side.
